key_insight: Swarmlet couples GPU-resident vortex-particle aerodynamics with flight dynamics and control to simulate interacting multirotors while conserving total vorticity and linear impulse.
engineering_relevance: The solver supports wake-aware analysis of multirotor performance and controlled formations, with a 100-quadrotor demonstration on one GPU.
method: Meshless reformulated vortex particle LES with evolving compact-support cores and an unregularized multipole far field.
Dynamic eddy viscosity via core spreading and conservative exchange, plus conservative strength relaxation.
Three rotor-model fidelities coupled to six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control, with connected circulation shedding.
evidence_signal: Reported results include agreement with direct summation to 5×10⁻⁷, third-order time convergence, hover thrust within 2% without calibration, and calibrated thrust/torque within 3.2% with near-wake relative L² differences of 0.08–0.21 against PIV.
watch_item: The 100-vehicle demonstration uses a coarser setting, so single-GPU swarm feasibility does not establish validation-level wake accuracy at that scale.
paper_title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
